official_finding_or_allegation: MCST states that it annually inspects copyright trust-management organizations on royalty collection and distribution, organizational management and operation, and accounting and fund management, and can issue improvement orders under the Copyright Act.
how_it_affects_music_claim: This supports including domestic rights governance as part of the music claim because the state itself treats trust-management governance as a recurring public-interest oversight issue rather than a one-off controversy.

official_finding_or_allegation: MCST found that KOMCA executives selected former and current affiliated companies as event contractors, paid directing fees and appearance or sponsorship payments from KOMCA accounts, and participated in ad-vendor evaluation while not avoiding use of their own songs in the ad; MCST states these acts violate the ethics code and implicate the Conflict of Interest Prevention Act and Improper Solicitation and Graft Act.
how_it_affects_music_claim: This is the strongest official basis for saying the domestic rights-management system cannot simply be treated as a neutral referee in foreign-platform disputes; governance opacity and self-dealing risk are part of the structural problem.

official_finding_or_allegation: MCST found that KOMCA created a KRW 700 million self-development budget item without general meeting or board approval and that executives and staff used corporate funds or the new item for gyms, dermatology, massage and similar spending that MCST describes as improper budget execution.
how_it_affects_music_claim: This directly supports the domestic governance-opacity layer by showing that royalty-funded general accounts were not always governed by transparent or properly approved controls.

official_finding_or_allegation: MCST found that KOMCA awarded facility contracts to an inexperienced company, had evaluation irregularities, entered contracts despite licensing-law problems, bypassed the national e-procurement system in some competitive bids, and found circumstances suggestive of concentrated work allocation.
how_it_affects_music_claim: This indicates broader internal-control weakness beyond royalty formulas, reinforcing the argument that domestic governance problems make foreign-platform disputes harder to verify and easier to politicize.

official_finding_or_allegation: MCST found that KOMCA effectively left election-management committee members in place for eight years without replacement, identified sponsorship spending patterns that could affect neutrality and fairness, and judged that KOMCA had still not implemented the long-running government improvement order to expand regular-membership representation.
how_it_affects_music_claim: This supports the claim that domestic rights administration has democratic-legitimacy and neutrality problems that bear directly on trust in royalty governance and industry representation.

official_finding_or_allegation: MCST found that Hamkkehaneun Eumak Jeojakin Hyeophoe failed to disclose general-meeting and board resolutions within the required time or disclosed them incorrectly and lacked fixed recruitment rules, creating risk that hiring would proceed opaquely.
how_it_affects_music_claim: This shows that governance-transparency risk is not confined to a single organization, so the domestic-governance layer should not be framed as a KOMCA-only anomaly.

official_finding_or_allegation: MCST found that the Recording Industry Association of Korea had inadequate overseas-trip documentation, paid travel expenses after regulatory deadlines, failed to verify applicants' career history in hiring, overlapped document and interview screeners, used only internal interviewers, and processed important organizational matters by written board resolution in violation of its articles.
how_it_affects_music_claim: This broadens the governance finding across multiple trust-management bodies and supports using `domestic governance opacity` as a system-level layer in the music reanalysis.

official_finding_or_allegation: MCST states that it will issue improvement orders, inspect compliance, pursue stronger disclosure of remuneration and allowances, and expand public-related-entity designation to additional trust-management organizations.
how_it_affects_music_claim: This supports treating governance opacity as a live institutional variable with policy consequences, not just an isolated historical criticism.
